findings.title: Deleting a run orphans its logs rows (control plane documents delete as '+data')
evidence: server/benchd.py:661 - `for t in ("phases", "telemetry", "events", "artifacts"):` - the child-table purge omits `logs` (and any `commands` rows tied to the run)
server/benchd.py:663 - `self.store.ex("DELETE FROM runs WHERE id=?")` removes the parent run row, leaving `logs.run_id` dangling
server/benchd.py SCHEMA (~lines 89-140) declares no FOREIGN KEY / ON DELETE CASCADE and the file sets no `PRAGMA foreign_keys`, so nothing cascades
docs/CONTROL_PLANE.md:132 - table row says `DELETE /runs/<id>` = 'delete a run (+data)'
tests/test_control_plane.py:285-287 - the delete test only asserts the run returns 404; it never checks that logs were removed

Reproduced (in-process benchd, temp SQLite): POST /runs -> POST /runs/<id>/log {lines:[orphan-canary-line]} -> DELETE /runs/<id> (200) -> GET /api/v1/runs/<id>/logs still returned HTTP 200 with the line; `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM logs WHERE run_id=?` stayed 1
findings.impact: Every deleted run keeps its full live-console history retrievable at `/api/v1/runs/<id>/logs`, the SQLite DB grows without bound, and the documented 'delete a run (+data)' contract is false. The logs route also serves a run the UI reports as gone, so the delete API silently under-delivers.
findings.recommendation: Add `logs` (and `commands` WHERE run_id) to the purge loop in `do_DELETE`, or add an FK with `ON DELETE CASCADE` plus `PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON`. Extend test_control_plane's delete case to assert `GET /runs/<id>/logs` and the `logs` table are empty after DELETE. Reconcile CONTROL_PLANE.md:132 with the resulting behaviour.

findings.title: README preset table documents 11 of the 13 shipped presets; 'Graphics only (FurMark/Valley)' is undocumented
evidence: README.md:210-220 - the Presets table has 11 rows (Quick check ... Full-system soak (long))
server/web/app.js:14-27 - `const PRESETS = { ... }` defines 13 entries, including app.js:23 'Graphics only (FurMark/Valley)' and app.js:16 'Stabilized full soak (15 min)'
bench/gui.py PRESETS and bench/tui.py PRESETS each expose 13 entries (verified by loading both modules with the repo venv)
tests/test_presets.py:12-28 - CANON enumerates 13 canonical presets, so 13 is the intended set
README.md contains no occurrence of 'Graphics only'; 'Stabilized full soak' appears only in prose (README.md:114-119), not in the preset table
findings.impact: The preset table is the operator-facing feature list; it understates what the GUI/TUI/web actually offer, and an entire preset (a 30 s FurMark/Valley graphics-only run) is discoverable only from the code/UI. New users may believe 'Video / graphics' is the only render option.
findings.recommendation: Update README.md:210-220 to list all 13 presets (or generate the table from `gui.PRESETS` in CI). Add 'Graphics only (FurMark/Valley)' to the docs and note it in the Dashboards/Updates sections.

findings.title: README advertises 'Release v1.1.0' while VERSION and the HEAD tag are 1.11.3
evidence: README.md:12 - `**Release \`v1.1.0\`**`
VERSION file contains `1.11.3`; `git log -1` at the audited commit shows tag `v1.11.3` on HEAD b9167095
.github/workflows/release.yml:81-94 - the release job only rewrites `VERSION` (`printf ... > VERSION`) and pushes a tag; it never edits README.md
AGENTS.md:192-207 - states the version is derived from `git describe --tags` and reported everywhere it matters
findings.impact: The repository's own headline document contradicts the release it ships. Anyone comparing README/`VERSION`/tags (or an implementation agent following README as the feature contract) gets a version that is 10 minor releases stale.
findings.recommendation: Either stop hard-coding the release in README (reference `VERSION`), or have release.yml update README.md alongside VERSION in the same commit. Reconcile the current text to 1.11.3.

findings.title: CONTROL_PLANE.md's command-support matrix is stale: it says the GUI/TUI fail update/restart, but they implement them
evidence: docs/CONTROL_PLANE.md:139-142 - 'the GUI/TUI dashboards implement start/stop/fan_curve/shutdown/reboot and the remote terminal (exec/shell), and fail update/power_limit/restart'
bench/gui.py:647-655 - gui.py handles `update`, `update_toolkit`, `iso_fetch`, `iso_write`, `iso_write_slot` and `restart`; only `power_limit`/unknown kinds ack 'unsupported'
bench/tui.py:296-304 - tui.py handles the same `update*`/`iso_*` set and `restart`; only unknown kinds ack 'unsupported'
findings.impact: The documented capability matrix understates the dashboards. An operator (or an implementation agent planning feature work) would wrongly assume a GUI/TUI runner cannot self-update or restart, and might duplicate already-shipped functionality.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite docs/CONTROL_PLANE.md:139-142 to match gui.py/_remote_command and tui.py/_apply_remote: dashboards implement start/stop/fan_curve/shutdown/reboot, update/update_toolkit/iso_*, restart, and exec/shell; only power_limit is unsupported. Add a parity test if practical.

findings.title: Committed prior-audit finding CI-P3-001 claims there are no CI workflows, but three exist at HEAD
evidence: docs/audits/repo-deep-dive/20261007-1731-main-4ecee97/findings.json:120 - evidence text 'No .github/ directory or workflow files are present in the repository' (finding CI-P3-001, status 'open')
At HEAD b9167095 `git ls-files .github` lists three workflows: .github/workflows/release.yml, .github/workflows/build-iso.yml, .github/workflows/build-app.yml
README.md:158-168 and AGENTS.md:242-247 describe those workflows as active (ISO/app builds on push)
findings.impact: A committed audit artifact contradicts the repository it lives in. Because the shared rules treat stale 'verified/absent' claims as defects, anyone reading the audit register re-does settled work and cannot trust the register's status column.
findings.recommendation: Mark CI-P3-001 as `verified-fixed` in the follow-up register / roadmap with the workflow paths as the closing artifact, or annotate that it is bounded to commit 4ecee97. Add a lint/CI check that flags audit claims whose evidence paths no longer match the tree.

findings.title: Documented test command (python tests/run_all.py) fails on stock Windows Python because curses is unguarded
evidence: README.md:310-312 - '`python tests/run_all.py          # RESULT: PASS`' and 'Stdlib only'
bench/tui.py:15 - `import curses` is unguarded; `curses` is not part of the Python standard library on Windows
tests/test_presets.py:40-41 - loads tui.py (and gui.py) with importlib, so the curses import executes

Observed: `python tests/run_all.py` with the system interpreter -> 'RESULT: FAIL (2)' including 'test_presets: crashed (No module named \'_curses\')'; `.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe tests/run_all.py` -> 'RESULT: PASS'
findings.impact: A Windows contributor following README/AGENTS.md literally sees a red suite through no fault of their change, and the 'stdlib only' claim is not literally true for the test entrypoint on Windows. It also masks real failures behind an environment crash.
findings.recommendation: State the exact command (the bootstrapped `.venv`, which contains `windows-curses`) in README/AGENTS.md, and/or make `tests/run_all.py` skip/fake the curses import when `import curses` fails, reporting a clear 'SKIP (needs windows-curses)' instead of a crash.

findings.title: Working tree at audit time diverges from the recorded commit (uncommitted source + test changes)
evidence: `git status --porcelain` at 2026-10-13T04:26-04:00: `M server/benchd.py`, `M server/import_results.py`, `M server/web/app.js`, `M tests/test_control_plane.py`, `M live/airootfs/usr/local/bin/bench-agent-env`; `git log -1` = b9167095 (the brief's commit)

`git show HEAD:server/benchd.py` contains none of `MAX_BODY`, `secrets.compare_digest`, or `os.path.commonpath`; the working-tree file does (MAX_BODY at line 55, compare_digest at 569, commonpath at 1254)

The set of modified files grew during the audit (test_control_plane.py and app.js appeared after the first observation) and the diffs contain coherent fixes plus matching test updates, i.e. looks like concurrent in-flight work rather than a static defect at HEAD
findings.impact: The commit named by the brief does not match the artifact set on disk, so `path:line` citations taken from the working tree may not resolve at the tagged commit, and the suite's result depends on which revision is loaded. Any audit/verification claim must therefore state its revision.
findings.recommendation: Audit a clean checkout pinned to the commit (or record the working-tree hashes), and land the in-flight changes so the branch tip equals the tree under review. Report the tree hash alongside every finding that cites server/benchd.py or import_results.py.

## Audit Metadata

- Audit name: repo-deep-dive
- Run: 20261013-0426-main-b916709
- Repository: `C:\temp\bench-test` (MaineCyberTech/bench-test)
- Branch: main
- Commit SHA: b9167095b08c2f45a814e88e09d88decbd0ea885 (tag `v1.11.3`)
- Generated at: 2026-10-13T04:35:00-04:00
- Auditor: domain subagent `03_feature_implementation_map`
- Area code: FEAT
- Output path: docs/audits/{name}/{run}/03_feature_implementation_map.md
- Scope limitations: read-only; no lab, no live-USB boot, no real benchmark run. The working tree was **dirty**
  and changed during the audit (see FEAT finding 7), so line numbers for `server/benchd.py` / `import_results.py`
  describe the working tree at the timestamps noted, not necessarily the tagged commit. No secrets were read.

## Scope

Reviewed the full feature surface a "feature implementation map" covers: web UI pages/tabs
(`server/web/`), API routes (`server/benchd.py` `do_GET`/`do_POST`/`do_DELETE`), the control-plane client
(`bench/benchreport.py`), runners/agents (`bench/agent.py`, `gui.py`, `tui.py`, `run_win.py`,
`Run-*.ps1`/`Run-LinuxBench.sh`), workers/jobs (scheduler + reapers), database entities (SQLite schema),
permissions/auth tiers, audit/event logs, the test suite (`tests/`), docs (`docs/`, `README.md`,
`AGENTS.md`) and the committed audit artifacts under `docs/audits/`.

Not reviewed: the actual benchmark math in the GPU/CPU/RAM/disk phases beyond their group wiring; the
PowerShell-heavy sensor paths; the ISO build end-to-end; anything requiring hardware, the lab, or a
network. SaaS domains named in the brief (billing, multi-tenant RLS, webhook delivery, mobile/PWA
analytics) are **not applicable** — this is a stdlib workstation-benchmark + fleet control plane, no
web framework, no database ORM, no billing, and the web UI is a single vanilla-JS page.

## Evidence Reviewed

- `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `VERSION`, `docs/CONTROL_PLANE.md`, `docs/DATA.md`, `docs/FUTURE_WORK.md`
- `server/benchd.py` (routes, auth, schema, scheduler, reapers), `server/web/app.js` + `index.html` + `style.css`,
  `server/import_results.py`
- `bench/agent.py`, `bench/gui.py`, `bench/tui.py`, `bench/benchreport.py` (command dispatch, PRESETS,
  `extra_runner_args`, `GROUPS`)
- `tests/run_all.py`, `tests/harness.py`, `tests/test_control_plane.py`, `tests/test_presets.py`
- `.github/workflows/release.yml`, `.github/workflows/build-iso.yml`, `.github/workflows/build-app.yml`
- `docs/audits/repo-deep-dive/20261007-1731-main-4ecee97/findings.json`

## Verification Performed

| Evidence | Type | Why relevant | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `git log -1`, `git status --porcelain` | command | Bind the audit to a revision | HEAD = b9167095; tree dirty (5 files) |
| `python tests/run_all.py` (system) | command | Reproduce README's `RESULT: PASS` | `RESULT: FAIL (2)` incl. `_curses` crash |
| `.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe tests/run_all.py` | command | Intended interpreter | `RESULT: PASS` |
| in-process benchd repro (POST run/log, DELETE run, GET logs) | command | Reproduce run-delete data loss | logs row survives delete (HTTP 200) |
| `preset_count.py` loading gui/tui/app.js | command | Count shipped presets | gui/tui/web = **13**, README table = **11** |
| `grep`/`Select-String` over routes, docs, tests | read | Map UI↔API↔docs | see Inventory |
| `git show HEAD:server/benchd.py` vs working tree | command | Self-consistency | HEAD lacks the working-tree fixes |

## Executive Summary

This is a **feature-complete, unusually well-wired** toolkit for its size. The three dashboards
(GUI, curses TUI, web) share one preset model and are kept in lock-step by `tests/test_presets.py`; the
control plane implements the documented REST+SSE+SQLite surface almost one-for-one; the agent handles
**every** command kind; and every documented reader (Runner identity, telemetry aliases, hardware
verdicts, derived stats) maps to real code. The stdlib test suite passes (`RESULT: PASS`) under the repo's
own `.venv` and covers API auth, per-runner keys, runs/phases/telemetry/logs/artifacts/stats, commands,
schedules, delete, reapers and SSE.

The gaps are at the seams, not in the core:

1. **One real functional defect** — `DELETE /api/v1/runs/<id>` purges phases/telemetry/events/artifacts
   but **not `logs`** (reproduced), contradicting `docs/CONTROL_PLANE.md:132` ("delete a run (+data)") and
   leaving orphaned rows that are still served by `/runs/<id>/logs`.
2. **Documentation drift** — the README preset table lists 11 of 13 presets and never mentions the
   `Graphics only (FurMark/Valley)` preset; the README's headline release is `v1.1.0` while `VERSION`
   and the HEAD tag say `1.11.3`; `CONTROL_PLANE.md` says the GUI/TUI fail `update`/`restart` when they
   in fact implement them; and a committed prior-audit finding claims the repo has no CI while three
   workflows exist.
3. **Repro/portability** — the documented `python tests/run_all.py` crashes on stock Windows Python
   (`No module named '_curses'`) unless run from the bootstrapped `.venv`.
4. **Revision binding** — the working tree at audit time contained uncommitted source + test changes not
   present at b9167095, so the audited commit and the artifact set disagree.

Recommended next actions: fix the run-delete purge (+ test), then a single docs-sync pass (README
presets, README release, CONTROL_PLANE command matrix, audit register), and make the test entrypoint
explicit for Windows.

## Detailed Review

### Item: Run deletion (`DELETE /api/v1/runs/<id>`)

- Evidence: `server/benchd.py:661-663`; `docs/CONTROL_PLANE.md:132`; `tests/test_control_plane.py:285-287`.
- What it does: removes `phases`, `telemetry`, `events`, `artifacts` for the run, then the `runs` row.
- How it appears to work: `for t in ("phases","telemetry","events","artifacts")` then `DELETE FROM runs`.
- Dependencies: schema has no FK/cascade; nothing else deletes `logs`.
- Current controls: run row 404s after delete; SSE publishes a `run deleted` event.
- Missing controls: `logs` (and `commands` keyed by `run_id`) are not purged; response is still 200.
- Risks: unbounded DB growth; deleted-run console history remains retrievable.
- Recommended improvement: include `logs` (and run-scoped `commands`) in the purge, or add a cascading FK.
- Suggested tests: assert `logs` count = 0 and `/runs/<id>/logs` is empty after DELETE.
- Suggested docs: align `CONTROL_PLANE.md:132` with the chosen semantics.
